changes.note: The ledger begins. Every tracked value and file as the branch stood at this commit.
Contacts keyed by job: sales to Eric, business and design partners to Kyle, operations to Peter, public collaboration to Tom. Team portraits and the real pull request exchange added.
Daylight stills for five industry pages, and three for the SMB and edge page to turn through. The desk box still now serves pricing only.
The Press and investors card says Email the CEO. Business and design partners stays under Partnerships.

Two team lines changed on their owners' word: Tom Turney's is his own wording, Thomas Braun's says patented and links the patent. A third payback scenario counts in tokens per joule, with a graph of every ladder rung.

Renamed to Metrale on every surface a visitor reads, with a placeholder wordmark until the kit lands. The old /why address redirects. Metrale Prime, the site's guide, is wired in behind primeEndpoint.

The Metrale kit applied: the M mark and wordmark from the kit's own geometry, its ground, inks and three hues in the tokens, Urbanist for words with Plex Mono kept for numbers, the kit's icons and cards. Metrale Prime's glyph is the mark.
Metrale kit applied: wordmark and mark drawn from the kit geometry, tokens, Urbanist, icons, social cards and the film's title cards re-rendered; Metrale Prime guide added
The film's closing button takes the kit's violet with ink text; light theme hue text darkened for the chips; developer nav Star button reads ink on violet
The six console clips re-recorded from the mockup with the Metrale lockup; the film re-cut from them; the About page explains the name

Solutions grouped by sector with a jump bar; how the control plane is built and the economics arithmetic, proposed; the team and the founders' doors held back, role mailboxes at metrale.com; Toyota on the wall, Synopsys off it

Two public sector pages, police and local government, each with a still; the three owners table, the metering block and the operator view, proposed; the labs call to action lands on the booking form; the developer control page points into the platform
Standalone repository: removed the unused static/brand links to the engine's old artwork and the blog's card, which lives with the blog
